The project

DOMUS grew out of a simple community idea: bring people together through small gatherings hosted in local homes. Built as a team project at WildHacks 2026, it connects people looking for a dinner or cultural event with hosts willing to share their table.

The product supports both sides of a gathering. Guests browse events and request to join; hosts create events and review requests. Profiles, calendars, and messaging help turn an event listing into a plan people can follow through on.

Context
WildHacks 2026 team project
Product
Hosts, guests, and local gatherings
Foundation
React, TanStack, and Supabase

The gathering has two sides

Browse as a guest

Explore events with filters, city suggestions, and distance-aware browsing. Open the event details and request a place.

Organize as a host

Create a gathering, review guest profiles and join requests, and track host commitments through the dashboard and calendar.

Stay connected

Match threads and unread-message helpers support conversation. The calendar separates hosting from attending.

How it works

The application combines typed routes and forms with Supabase-backed authentication and data. Event, user, join-request, and message relationships support the host and guest flows.

  1. Interface and routes

    React and TanStack provide event browsing, profiles, dashboards, calendars, and messages.

  2. Application logic

    Forms, domain types, matching rules, and shared state connect the guest and host journeys.

  3. Backend services

    Supabase supplies authentication and data services. Optional integrations support maps, geocoding, and assistant features.

The repository credits its frameworks, UI primitives, starter configuration, and external APIs alongside DOMUS-specific application work.

A key decision

Make a request a clear step in the journey.

Browsing an event and joining it are different actions. A guest requests a place, and a host reviews the profile before approving the request.

That structure gives the product a recognizable progression: discover a gathering, request to join, then coordinate. The interface needs to work for both the person opening their home and the person looking for a community.

What belongs to the project

The public README documents DOMUS-specific product flows, copy, styling, application logic, and data integration choices. It also identifies reused foundations such as React, TanStack, Supabase, Radix UI, and shadcn/ui patterns.

This page presents the hackathon project as team work. The repository is the place to explore the implementation and its dependency acknowledgments.
